lens: Adversarial critique — over-engineering / simpler-path, WITHIN the fixed fully-native constraint (custom skills + Harmony HQ tabs are non-negotiable; the attack is on unnecessary complexity inside that path). Grounded in the Build 3672 decomp notes, reflection-dump-2026-09-01, DECISIONS.md D9-D14, the existing v2 code in mod/StoreManager/Scripts/, and the two prior adversarial reviews (07/08).
verdict: The native path is fine; the plan over-builds inside it. Runtime SkillData is the right call (don't let a bundle back in). But the plan then re-adds cost the native decision didn't require: a SECOND Harmony-built HQ tab, a THIRD custom skill for Assistant Manager whose entire effect is +1/+1, a 7-field Department record with spatial shelf-tagging and a three-tier trim algorithm, and 2-3 redundant mechanisms per wiring concern. Ship Store Manager only for the first native release (one skill, one tab), fold Team Leader + a 5-field department model into it as release two, and never mint sm:skill_assistantmanager. That cuts roughly half the new surface with no loss the user will notice.
topIssues: Two Harmony-built HQ tabs double the single highest-risk surface in the mod. The prior review (07) already called ONE injected BizMan tab 'highest-risk, lowest-value': it needs a SetUpTabs postfix, a blind clone of the live PurchasingAgents prefab hierarchy (RectTransform anchors + TextLocalizationComponent + Button + TMP on one GO — not in the decomp), insertion into the private _tabs list (BizManBusiness.cs:166 kicks the user off a tab not in _tabs), and a hand-rolled ScrollRect/Viewport/VerticalLayoutGroup/ContentSizeFitter MonoBehaviour. The plan builds ALL of that twice. Team Leader is conceptually a child of Store Manager (manager -> store -> department -> TL), so a peer 'Team Leiders' tab also forces TeamLeaderTabView to re-establish the store/manager context the Store Managers tab already holds.

Assistant Manager as a third custom SkillData is pure cost. The plan itself gives it no plan and no tab — its whole mechanical effect is '+1 MaxStores, +1 TL capacity' on StoreManagerPlan.AssistantManagerEmployeeId. That is a checkbox. Every minted skill is another uninstall landmine (risk list: vanilla SkillHelper.GetData NPEs on the player's save — wage calc, employee card, CompatibilityFixes — if the mod is removed while custom-skill employees exist) and another full pass through RecruitmentWiring + HqDeskWiring + Locales + wage tuning, for a title string. The user's explicit mandate is TWO roles (Filiaalmanager + Team Leader); Assistant Manager is community-chat hierarchy colour, not in that mandate.

The Department model carries three subsystems the 'TL flags stock, manager approves' loop does not need: (a) ShelfInstanceIds spatial tagging — the research itself says instance ids churn on remodel and the self-healing fallback IS the product-name list, so it is cost with zero loop value; (b) per-department Priority plus a three-tier over-budget trim (priority desc -> pro-rata within band -> primary-products-first) tuning a loop nobody has playtested — exactly the 'can't be tuned without playtest, shouldn't gate v1' pattern review 07 flagged for MistakeModel; (c) a two-option seeding flow (all-primary AND auto-split-N).

Redundant wiring layers, each 'OR' being code to build/test/maintain. HQ-desk skill support has THREE mechanisms specced: suitableSkills array append + a Harmony prefix on ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation + a skipScheduleCheck degrade. Recruitment has the two required array appends PLUS an optional Harmony postfix on BusinessTypeHelper.OnBusinessTypesLoaded that just duplicates the city-load call. HQ capacity has two formulas (GetAssignableItems().Count OR 1+floor(squareMeters/X)). The plan also specs an optional BizManBusiness.Awake anti-flicker postfix it then admits is 'not required'.

Phase A is not a minimal proof milestone. It is ~12 file touches (SkillRegistry, 2 Harmony patch files, RecruitmentWiring, HqDeskWiring, GameApi, StoreManagerPlan, Locales x2, Commands, Options, Core) before the first in-game check that a runtime custom skill even survives a save-load / city reload — the one thing the whole native bet rests on and the thing the research is least certain about (Skills dict wiped and rebuilt every city load, no mod-merge; BuildTagCache internals not in the decomp).

Re-parenting the supervision logic onto the new skill is the moment to drop the v2 ContractSnapshot / OriginalContract / PendingRestore deferred-restore-past-Monday-lock machinery (already in StoreManagerPlan.cs and DeliveryContracts.cs). Review 07 already said cut it: on detach, contract enabled=false + a toast is enough; the snapshot/restore + pending-drain state is parity-chasing PricingManagerPlan.originalStorePrices for a case the player rarely hits.
recommendedChanges: KEEP runtime ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>() — do NOT switch to an AssetBundle. SkillHelper.Skills is wiped and rebuilt via OnSkillDataLoaded on every save-load / new-game / city-load with no mod-merge step, so a bundle needs the identical re-injection AND adds a Unity-version-locked build artifact and Addressables load path. Runtime construction is the simpler path; the plan got this right. The only asset ever needed is a flat PNG via Sprite.Create for icon28, and that is already optional Phase D.

First native release = Store Manager ONLY: one custom skill (sm:skill_storemanager), one Harmony HQ tab. Re-parent the v2 supervision loop onto it verbatim MINUS the snapshot/restore machinery (detach = enabled=false + toast).

Phase C: ship Team Leader + department management as a drill-down SECTION inside the Store Managers tab (manager -> store -> departments -> assign TL). Build the dedicated 'Team Leiders' tab only as Phase D polish, after the single-tab SetUpTabs postfix has proven stable in the wild. One BuildTab path, one TabView MonoBehaviour for the first two releases.

Cut sm:skill_assistantmanager entirely. Model Assistant Manager as a promotion flag on an existing hire — a Team Leader (sm:skill_teamleader) with IsAssistant=true on the plan, giving +1 store cap / +1 TL capacity. No third SkillData, no third wiring pass, no third uninstall-cleanup case. Revisit a distinct skill only if playtest says the title matters.

Reduce Department to { Name, StoreAddress, List<string> ProductItemNames, string TeamLeaderEmployeeId, bool Dormant }. Cut ShelfInstanceIds. Cut Priority. Over-budget trim = flat pro-rata across all requested lines — one rule. Seeding = one option only (one department = all primary products from GetPrimaryProducts()); the player edits membership afterward. Keep the 'store with no departments = one implicit whole-store department on the proven v2 ComputeTarget path' fallback.

Collapse the redundant wiring. Desk support = the suitableSkills array append only (it is how the vanilla manager skills already sit on ba:itemname_desktopcomputer/laptop/computer); keep skipScheduleCheck as the degrade; build the HasSkillForWorkstation prefix only if the append is observed to fail in-game. Recruitment = the two array appends called from city load; drop the OnBusinessTypesLoaded postfix. HQ capacity = desk count (GetAssignableItems().Count) only; drop the squareMeters formula. Drop the BizManBusiness.Awake anti-flicker postfix.

Split Phase A. Milestone A1 = SkillRegistry (SM only) + the GetData postfix on both overloads + the two recruitment array appends + the desk array append + Locales entry + flip GameApi.ManagerSkill to sm:skill_storemanager. Stop and do the in-game check: skill survives save-load AND a city reload, appears in the Agency dropdown with the HQ business selected, hire shows correct title + wage, no 'Skill not found' spam. Everything else currently in Phase A becomes A2.

KEEP (these are cheap and load-bearing, not over-engineering): the GetData postfix on both overloads (crash-safety net for the ~15 unguarded call sites); the RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate direct-call fallback action (doubles as the test surface review 07 praised); the build-number gate [3600,3899] + non-null-handle checks + degrade-to-ModOptions-panel; D18's refusal to mutate BuildingSize/BuildingVersion; the D12-safe request math (amountOrderedLastWeek + stock gap, never the contract line's own amount); the OnUnloadAsync re-skill-to-ba:skill_purchasingagent cleanup.
v1ScopeRecommendation: First native release: Store Manager only — one custom skill, one Harmony HQ tab. sm:skill_storemanager built at runtime via ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData> (secondarySkill=string.Empty, non-null gradient, BuildTagCache in try/catch), re-injected on a SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded postfix + a city-load backstop, with a defense-in-depth GetData postfix on both overloads. Hireability = append the id to HQ BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills + every RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills + the three HQ desk items' suitableSkills, all idempotent, all re-applied each city load. The v2 supervision loop (mod-owned StoreManagerPlan in GameInstance.modData, Saturday weekly pass, DeliveryContract restock within WeeklyRestockBudgetCap, feedback, read-only-on-corrupt) re-parented onto it unchanged except: drop ContractSnapshot/OriginalContract/PendingRestore — detach just sets enabled=false + toasts. One 'Store Managers' BizMan tab via a single BizManBusiness.SetUpTabs postfix (clone the live PurchasingAgents sibling, insert into _tabs, SetActive), gated on build number + non-null handles, with the existing Options->Mods panel as the permanent fallback UI. Release two: sm:skill_teamleader + a 5-field Department record (Name, StoreAddress, ProductItemNames, TeamLeaderEmployeeId, Dormant) + flat pro-rata over-budget trim, all managed as a drill-down inside the Store Managers tab. Post-v1, only if playtest asks: dedicated 'Team Leiders' tab, per-department Priority, shelf-instance tagging, and any Assistant Manager tier. Never mint sm:skill_assistantmanager — model it as an IsAssistant flag on a Team Leader.
mustVerifyInGameFirst: Does SkillData.BuildTagCache() on a runtime CreateInstance<SkillData> throw or leave HasTag() unreliable? TaggedScriptableObject/TagRef internals are in an un-decompiled assembly.

Does the private SkillHelper.Skills reflection injection land before the first consumer after a city load, or is there a window where candidate generation / wage calc NPEs? Specifically: is the GetData postfix alone sufficient for crash-safety, making the dict injection only a discoverability concern (headhunter dropdown, EmployeeFilterController chips)?

Does appending sm:skill_storemanager to ba:itemname_desktopcomputer/laptop/computer suitableSkills actually let the custom-skill manager take an HQ-desk WorkShift (ScheduleHelper.HasSkillForWorkstation), and does the append survive the Addressables reload on each city load?

Is RecruitmentAgencySettings one shared Addressable asset or per-building copies, and does the agency skill dropdown = employeePrimarySkills INTERSECT availableEmployeeSkills actually surface the appended id with the HQ business selected?

Cloning the live PurchasingAgents menu-button prefab blind: does the button render correctly (RectTransform anchors, TextLocalizationComponent + Button + TMP on one GameObject, menu layout group), and does inserting the id into private _tabs keep the player from being kicked off it (BizManBusiness.cs:166) across a business-dropdown switch and a save reload?

Uninstall path: with an sm:skill_storemanager employee in the save, does removing the mod NPE vanilla SkillHelper.GetData in wage calc / the employee card, and does OnUnloadAsync's re-skill-to-ba:skill_purchasingagent cleanup actually run before serialize?

Wage: runtime dump of vanilla ba:skill_customerservice / ba:skill_purchasingagent / ba:skill_hrmanager baseHourlyWage so the mod's baseHourlyWage constant lands the hire near the intended ~$30 without guesswork.
